rows.grounds: not exceeding the nature of consciousness
because they cannot be non-conscious and because no separate possessor can be established

items.question: Why can the powers such as action not be separate from consciousness?
premises: The powers beginning with action are not beyond the nature of consciousness.
They cannot be joined to a non-conscious nature.
No separate possessor of these powers can be established.
items.inference: Therefore the powers such as action are not independent entities but remain within consciousness.
uncertainties: The exact force of adhikā in saṃvidrūpādhikā is slightly compressed in translation.
items.plain_english: The powers beginning with action do not go beyond the nature of consciousness. They cannot belong to something non-conscious, and no separate owner of them can be established.

rows.grounds: in the teaching of the Supreme Lord
unlike the unseen principle posited by the followers of Kanada
a separate substrate for powers conceived as attributes

items.question: Does the Supreme Lord's teaching posit a separate substrate for the powers?
premises: In the scripture of the Supreme Lord, no separate substrate for the powers is taught.
The powers are not treated like attributes requiring an external support.
This differs from the unseen principle posited in the Kanada school.
items.inference: Therefore the powers do not depend on an external substrate distinct from consciousness.
uncertainties: kāṇādadṛṣṭivat is taken as an analogy to the Vaisheshika unseen principle; the verse is compressed.
items.plain_english: In the teaching of the Supreme Lord, no separate support is posited for the powers, unlike the unseen principle assumed by the followers of Kanada.

rows.grounds: the powers of seeing, action, will, and so on
if those powers were truly separate

items.question: What follows if seeing, action, and will are taken as separate powers?
premises: Seeing, action, will, and the other powers would be treated as mutually separate.
Shiva is affirmed as one reality.
A statement of unity becomes empty if its powers are made fundamentally separate.
items.inference: Therefore the powers cannot be ultimately separate if Shiva is truly one.
items.plain_english: If seeing, action, will, and the other powers were really separate, then saying that Shiva is one would become an empty phrase with no real meaning.

rows.grounds: freedom is nothing other than consciousness

items.question: What is freedom when it is examined closely?
premises: Freedom is identical with consciousness itself.
When examined, that same freedom appears in multiple forms.
These multiple forms are the various powers.
items.inference: Therefore the many powers are expressions of the one freedom of consciousness.
items.plain_english: So freedom is nothing other than consciousness itself. When examined, that same freedom resolves into the many powers.

rows.grounds: because liberation is the manifestation of the Self
therefore this doubt should not arise here
an effect produced from a cause
even someone who knows that cause-effect relation

items.question: Does knowing a cause-effect relation by itself guarantee liberation?
premises: Liberation is the manifestation of the Self.
A mere effect produced from a cause does not amount to that manifestation.
Knowing a cause-effect relation does not by itself bring liberation.
items.inference: Therefore liberation cannot be reduced to an ordinary causal product or to mere causal knowledge.
uncertainties: The compressed phrase kāraṇātkārya is read as denying a merely causal model of liberation.
items.plain_english: Since liberation is the manifestation of the Self, one should not think that merely knowing a cause and its effect is enough to make someone free.

rows.grounds: described as a cause producing a result

items.question: Is the relation between knowledge and liberation a primary cause-and-effect relation?
premises: Knowledge is said to be related to liberation as cause to result.
That causal description is not the primary or ultimate sense of their relation.
If the causal sense is not primary, the stated objection does not hold.
items.inference: Therefore the objection based on a strict cause-effect model of liberation is resolved.
items.plain_english: Although knowledge is spoken of as causing liberation, that is not the primary sense of their relation. So the objection raised on that basis does not stand.

rows.grounds: essentially of the nature of knowledge

items.question: Why does action appear so varied if it is essentially knowledge?
premises: Action is essentially of the nature of knowledge.
Within itself, action takes on a grosser form.
A grosser form allows manifold variation to appear.
items.inference: Therefore the diversity seen in action does not contradict its identity with knowledge.
items.plain_english: Action is in essence knowledge, but it takes on a grosser form. That is why such great variety is seen in it.

rows.grounds: of the methods included under the action-based means
distinguished by what is taken as inner or outer
because of many divisions and subdivisions, they become countless in their internal forms

items.question: Why do the action-based means become countless in practice?
premises: The action-based means contain many subsidiary methods.
These methods are divided according to inner and outer objects.
Their divisions and subdivisions multiply into great variety.
items.inference: Therefore the action-based means become countless in their internal forms.
uncertainties: avāntarāt is read as referring to internal or subsidiary differentiation.
items.plain_english: Within the means based on action, the methods are divided by inner and outer objects. Because of their many divisions and subdivisions, they become countless.

rows.grounds: that because the means differ, liberation too would differ

items.question: Does the diversity of means imply a diversity in liberation itself?
premises: Some thinkers suspected that different means would produce different liberations.
The previous explanation shows why the means can vary greatly.
Variation in means does not by itself establish variation in the final state.
items.inference: Therefore the suspicion that liberation differs according to the means is refuted.
items.plain_english: This also refutes what some wise people suspected: that because the means differ, liberation itself would also differ.

rows.grounds: through different causal modes involving impurity and the cessation of its concealing power
as in cases like the breaking of a pot, where causes may differ but the result is the same kind of destruction

items.question: Can different causes of liberation produce different kinds of liberation?
premises: Liberation may be described through different causal processes involving impurity and concealment.
Different causes do not always produce different kinds of result.
The analogy of a pot's destruction shows sameness of result despite causal variation.
items.inference: Therefore liberation is not made different in kind by differences in its causes.
uncertainties: The internal analysis of the long compound follows the general sense of impurity and concealment being removed.
items.plain_english: Even if the causes differ, such as through the destruction or cessation of impurity and its concealing power, liberation itself is not different, just as the destruction of a pot is the same kind of result even when brought about in different ways.

rows.grounds: in the scripture called Shri Purva
in the definitive explanation of penetration

items.question: Where is the threefold division of penetration authoritatively taught?
premises: A threefold division has been indicated.
This division is taught in the scripture named Shri Purva.
The teaching is given by the Supreme Lord in the context of determining penetration.
items.inference: Therefore the threefold classification of penetration has scriptural authority.
items.plain_english: This threefold division was taught by the Supreme Lord in the scripture called Shri Purva, in the section that determines the nature of penetration.

rows.grounds: of a person free from discursive thought
that is declared to be the Shambhava penetration

items.question: What kind of penetration is called Shambhava?
premises: A person may be free from discursive thought.
Such a person may be awakened by the teacher.
The penetration that arises in that condition is identified as Shambhava.
items.inference: Therefore Shambhava penetration arises through the teacher's awakening in a thought-free state.
items.plain_english: When a person who is free from discursive thought is awakened by the teacher, the penetration that arises is called the Shambhava penetration.
